I love fluffy paper clays, Crayola basic air dry clays, and Sculpey polymer clay glaze. This feels like none of them! It is pretty fluffy like a paper clay, as strong and stretchy as a putty or even slime, and is vibrantly colored without any weird toxic smells! Rather than use it for actual sculpting we have been using it with are kids with special needs! It is so soft and easy to stretch! It does not stick to hair, fabric, nor carpets! Once it starts to dry it becomes slightly more firm and rips like a putty rather than stretches like a slime.
Not all of the accessories matched what was shown, but we didn't really use very many of them either because we were using them for sensory play instead. The pack will last a very long time, but I will be replacing as soon as we need to!

Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary Ok. Here's the deal. If you actually order and receive the Elefun version produced with/through Hasbro as the current item listed as of this date shows, here's the real review by an adult:

There are 10 monkeys in a barrel. It is listed on the plastic, throw away wrapping. And that's what you get from this brand. 10. Each barrel has ten color corresponding monkeys.
About the monkeys: they are durable and not flimsy. The monkey's tails are part of the body and are not useable. All monkeys are the same mold.....BUT there are 2 each of different facial expressions. This is not so easy to notice while playing but yes, the monkeys are in facial pairs. All monkeys are the same size.

Now.....lol....from a serious player (lol) that grew up with the 60s, 70s versions: these monkeys have....two arms....one arm is bent closer to the head so it's open loop is a tad smaller. Meaning....it makes a differnece in how easy or hard it is to link them. Also....the hand shape....well....it isn't as pointed and hook like as it was years ago. So yes....it is harder and I think that's a reason there is only 10 now.

Is it fun? Yes. Worth the money?? To me....because a fast food meal costs this much. And replayablity is very high. Also....you can buy two and do color challenges. Or time two players....or lots of creativity to play.

I would rather have a reproduction of the original. BUT these are functional and in my honest review, more difficult to chain over 7; making for more competition.

I think this is a good product for children, teens, families and elderly.

**I also think this could help anyone with motor skill issues or be good for even Alzheimer persons who enjoy things simple and close up.

This is a good product.

The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games Stone Age [[VIDEOID:9645a95d436279cab83d9584b2798107]] In this video, I show one round of playing the game. The game is fast paced, and it's about an interesting time in human history.

This is a pretty fun game, but for me it got old really fast. I really like empire building games, like [[ASIN:B002L6HJCI Age of Empires]], so I thought I would love this. But, I just liked it, I didn't love it.

The problem is that there's really only one strategy to the game, which is this: Get as many civilization cards as you can, and try to spend 100% of your resources by the time the game ends.

Pros:
+If you love the stone age, then this is probably a pretty good game for you.
+It's a pretty fun game.
+If you have a group of super casual gamers, you'll probably enjoy this for a long time. But all it takes is one serious gamer to disrupt the game for everyone.
+The game goes by pretty quick, and gets quicker the more you've played it.

Cons:
-Scoring is a little confusing. You typically score about 200-350 points on a game, but the score only goes to 100.
-Limited strategies, since there really is only one strategy
-Not enough luck to make it fun for casual gamers
-I wish they would have play tested this game a little bit more. I got the feeling that if they would have changed a few things on the cards and scoring, it would have been an awesome game. For example, civilization cards are way too heavily weighted.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games Stone Age

The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.

Hasbro Gaming Deluxe Turntable Scrabble Remarkable. Scrabble is cool. Hep. Rad. Outta sight. But Scrabble in this deluxe form is sublime, intoxicating. The pieces stay put, thanks to little walls around each space. You can spin the board so as to not need to examine it upside down. The pieces never slide around. The plastic coating lets you wipe it off, unlike the cardboard version which stains. Nothing is compromised from the original, flat cardboard version, but everything is improved.

OK. Not everything. It still can't help you dump the Q, Z and J at the end of the game without a U. And it is unlikely to assist you in stopping your grandmother's amazing ability to squeeze you out of that triple word score you hoped to grab with a seven-letter word. Take that up with Gram. Just remember who made you the cookies.

Seriously, I recommend this to any family or commited Scrabble player. Families need it for that `full-body contact' style of play that sometimes happens with children or cats involved. Commited Scrabble players need it for pretty much the same reason!

I fully recommend this game.

Anthony Trendl
editor, HungarianBookstore.com

Just nothing with capitals or foreign words, unless of course, you are from somewhere else, but then, they aren't foreign any longer, are they?

Order up a serving of Scrabble. Figure out if you need this version or the deluxe version (which is mighty cool.) If you are new to Scrabble, this is the version to start with.

When you get the game in the mail, call up some friends, turn on some tunes, crack open something tasty and cold, and start munching a few chips. This ain't a game you gotta be smart to play. I've seen guys who only know small words, but they could see the best ways to use them. Vocabs don't win the game. Thinking on your feet will win the game.

I fully recommend Scrabble.

Anthony Trendl
[...]
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Scrabble Crossword Game

text_fidelity_a:
MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys The box says that this Magnet Building Sticks set is for ages six and up, but I'm really enjoying playing with it as an adult. I think younger kids would need some help to do the suggested building projects, but using the set to build things is easy. The set includes 120 magnetic sticks, 40 steel balls, and a gray bag with a drawstring to hold the set if you don't want to use the original packaging. The balls are 1 inch across, and the sticks are 2.25 inches long and 1/4 inch across.

The magnets hold together strong enough to basically stay where you put them but not so strong that it's difficult to pull things apart. The more stable builds (which have many triangles instead of squares) hold their shape well as you build them. Some of the building projects that have a more open structure have a tendency to collapse during certain stages of building, and then they start to attach to parts that they aren't supposed to. It can be a mess to straighten out. Once I realized that this could happen, I was more careful to stabilize these open structures as I built them, so this hasn't been a problem since.

The set also came with pictures of a number of projects. The pictures show only the finished building projects, but they were not always clear about what went where when the lines overlapped in the picture. Still, I've been able to do most of the projects, and of course you can come up with your own ideas. Kids may become frustrated trying to figure out the pictures and prefer to make their own building projects. Overall, I've had a lot of fun with this as have a teenager and a tween that have played with it.
text_fidelity_b: MONILON 160 Pcs Magnet Building Sticks Kids Toys, Lengthen Magnetic Construction Building Blocks Set 3D Brain Training Learning Educational DIY STEM Toys

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.

This little PW Jeep was easy to assemble, without any confusion or difficulty, and though the sticker additions are tedious, it's not hard & they peel off to restick if you mess up a little

So after assembling and decorating, there's battery charging. Your best option is to wait until the kiddos are sleeping to build and charge this. Or even better, do it at the grandparent's house! It takes quite a while to recharge, too, so I suggest purchasing a second battery to keep the fun going.

This is a fairly rigid frame that will protect the littles from any low-speed collisions. The specs say that this will hold 2 kids, aged 3-7, up to 130 lbs. I doubt you can fit two 75 lb 7-year-olds in this little Jeep, or you might need a pry bar to get them out! Maybe a couple 5-year-olds could fit ok. Mainly tall kids will have trouble getting into it. It's great for two preschoolers, though.

The two main fun features of this PW Jeep are the real lights on the "rollbar" and the dinosaur and chase sounds from the 'radio'! The awesome parental feature is the ability to set a slow speed for littles and increase to 5 mph as they learn better control. I also love the power-lock breaks that will stop this instantly if a little one steps on the pedal!

Loads of fun for the little raptor hunter!

text_fidelity_a: USA Toyz AstroShot Zero GS Shooting Games for Kids - Nerf Compatible Floating Ball Targets for Shooting with Foam Blaster Toy Gun, 10 Floating Ball Targets, 10 Foam Darts, and 5 Flip Shooting Targets I researched all of the products like this. I read all of the different reviews for all of the different products like this. I watched all of the youtube reviews of every product like this, including the Nerf one. This is the only one that had a quiet motor. All the rest had a motor that is super loud which can get annoying and distracting fast. Then I looked at how high the air blew the balls. This product was the only one that had air that blew the balls pretty high from the product. It also looked like an easy assembly. I bought this for a gift for my 9 year old nephew who likes shooting Nerf guns. I wanted to test it out first before wrapping it up. It was easy to assemble. All you have to do is place the orange ball holders into the product. Thats it. Then you place the balls on top and turn it on. The air lifts them at the height that you are wanting. Not close to the product where you would think "This kind of sucks". The motor really was nice and quiet. You can barely hear it. If youre looking to buy one of these air lifting ball target toys, this is the one you want. There is another product by the same company that is black in color, but the reviews for that one didnt look so good. So buy this one, the grey and orange one. Our test run went great. Everything worked as I was hoping. The balls stay floating. They dont lift and fall over time. They stay floating in the air. It comes with a gun but that gun is a single load gun, so you have to stop and reload it every time. So I would either purchase a separate Nerf gun if the person youre giving it to doesnt have one or if you already have one, use that instead. This is the one you want. I hope this helps!

QUOKKA Giant Outdoor Stacking Game for Family This package came with three wooden puzzles: Arctic animals, outer space, and construction trucks. Each puzzle has 26-28 pieces. The construction trucks puzzle is the simplest because it has the 26 pieces and it's obvious which pieces go to which truck. The animals puzzle is only a little more difficult. The outer space puzzle is more difficult unless you know the order of the planets. It would have been nice to have a picture of what you're putting together on that one. Each corner piece can be identified by words or such so that you know which corner to put it in. That helps the puzzle get started. There is a notch in the top, right corner to help you get started with pulling the pieces out (or, of course, you can turn it upside down). The backboard on the Arctic animals came slightly warped, but the others were fine. They do make a point of storing the puzzles between 40 and 60% humidity.

It looks like the pieces have been laser cut out of one piece of wood. The pieces are about 3 mm thick, and they feel sturdier than a cardboard puzzle. The picture has been lightly painted on the wood. Generally, the pieces are easy to pull apart and put together. The first time I worked the puzzle, some pieces were a little stuck together, but they seemed fine the second time. I got these for my four-years-old niece. These seem to be about the right level for her as the different pieces are different enough in shape and it's fairly clear what part of the picture is on them. The pieces were fitted together tightly enough, though, that she sometimes needed an adult to help properly align them to get them to fit. When you take the pieces out, the backboard is blank (no suggested shapes to help very young puzzle workers).
text_fidelity_b: QUOKKA Giant Outdoor Stacking Game for Family

The price tag alone made me walk away from it more than a few times when birthday shopping. I have since changed my mind. I am surprised to say that this is a very durable and entertaining toy. My tween daughter has had it for a few weeks now and has yet to grow tired of it. She loves that she can get it to listen to her commands (aka - claps) and respond. She can teach it tricks (sit, beg, dance, etc.) and she can play games with it. This little toy does quite a bit to keep your child entertained. It's great for young ones, too. There aren't any parts that come loose or appear to be a choking hazard.
Since we do not have a fijit, I cannot say how well the yippit "plays" with the fijit or responds. However, I am sure as the Christmas season gears up, you'll see these cute little toys on display everywhere interacting with each other. I would suggest, though, that you pick one up ASAP if your child has been requesting it. I have a feeling that this toy might be one of the first to sell out by Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Fijit Friends Yippits Scooch Figure (Blue)

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz Make sure you know what you are getting yourself into before purchasing this item. I think it is a great item for the right person/people. If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Break in™ Alcatraz

text_fidelity_a:
VTech Sit-to-Stand Alphabet Train I don't know about a kid being strangled by the alphabet train. I suppose it's possible as there is a dip in between the two pieces of the train. My problems, however, are just of a different nature. I think this may be one of the most poorly designed toys I've ever purchased for my toddler..
I bought the train on a whim because it was on sale. It's colorful, makes noise, blah blah blah. After a couple of weeks of use, I started to notice the flaws in the design of the toy, and you know it seems like VTech has a bad habit of just putting out colorful, noisy crap that they know parents will buy regardless if it's good quality and design or not.
First of all, the thing is LOUD. There are two "choices" for volume, but the one that's supposed to be quieter can be heard across our 2500 square foot house. This is a common toy problem; I believe that the idiots coming up with kids' toys do not actually HAVE children, or they would put a quieter setting on these toys so that parents aren't stuck in the "LET'S RIDE THE ALPHABET TRAIN!" hell day after day.
Second, the train is too freaking narrow. It's too easy to topple over, so when my still-a-bit-unsteady 14-month-old would try to get on it to "ride", he often fell over. Now he's a lot better with balance at 18 months, but the thing is still too narrow.
Third, the train is not designed well for riding at all. Yes, it has handles and a seat, but the design of them is pretty unusable until the kid is way too old to be playing with an alphabet train. I watched my toddler today try to get on the toy and ride it; where his little butt goes is where the hump in the train car is, and if he sat back far enough to get off the hump, he couldn't reach the handles. What the crap? My child is not a chimp and he's not Stretch Armstrong. Why are the engine and car so far apart?
Ugh. We're keeping the dang thing because he does like to put the blocks into the train and watch them shoot out the engine. But as far as usability, the alphabet recognition is really the only thing that the toy has accomplished. If I could go back in time, I'd never buy this stupid train.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Sit-to-Stand Alphabet Train

Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. This allows for a greater range of neck & head motion over other dolls of this size, which have completely cloth torsos and limited, if any, neck motion.

Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

Her mouth is a unique shape and expression, not common with dolls in this space. Her shoes are cute, and her hair is very shiny.
